newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farmers hope for another bumper grain crop.
newsitem.headline: French farmers hope for another bumper grain crop.

text.p: France's grain crop is ripening in ideal conditions after an earlier drought scare, and the harvest looks increasingly capable of coming in well above average, official crop analysts said.

With crops at the crucial filling-out stage -- when the weight of each individual grain will be defined in the last few weeks -- few are prepared to say whether French wheat farmers will manage to repeat last year's crop of the century.
But conditions are surprisingly similar to 1996, when northern France had a late surge in yields while the traditional wheat belt south of Paris limped behind after an early drought.
"We are looking at a beautiful crop. Maybe nearly as good as last year," said a government crop analyst in the northeastern Pas de Calais region, whose yields shattered records in 1996.
Mild temperatures and scattered moisture in the north are ideal for the final few weeks in which grain crops mature.
But high temperatures and strong, drying winds earlier this week in the bread-basket region of Beauce, south of Paris, have renewed fears of another below-average harvest there.
Last year's French wheat harvest was a record 34.7 million tonnes, 14 percent above the five-year average of 30.3 million.
Barley production was about average at 9.5 million tonnes, of which 6.8 million was winter barley sown the previous autumn.

Regional grain analysts polled by Reuters this week are confident wheat output will remain well above average, partly because of an area increase that looks set to conquer most yield damage caused by the second spring drought in a row.
But grain weight will define the last few million tonnes.

"The problem is last year we just didn't see these record yields almost until the last moment. Even veteran farmers didn't know what a crop they had until it was weighed at the silos," another grain official in northern France said.
Freak moisture in the first week of July gave last year's crop a sharp last-minute lift north of the river Seine.
Average wheat yields last year were 7.3 tonnes per hectare compared with a 1991-95 average of 6.7 tonnes.
This year's sown areas are up around three percent for wheat and seven percent for barley, but until recently the repeat drought had left farmers fearing a bad knock in yields.
Grain officials say the best point of comparison is the 1995 harvest, which had soft wheat yields of 6.6 tonnes per hectare.

Upgrading that figure by the average annual yield growth of 0.1 tonnes per hectare, and using the latest 1997 sowing figure of 4.951 million hectares, would indicate a potential 1997 harvest of 33.7 million tonnes, the officials said.
How much the final outcome varies will depend on weather in the next few weeks, but analysts said it would need a severe setback to throw the harvest completely off track now.
One senior French grain official doubted, however, that last year's exceptional wheat harvest would be bettered this summer.
France is Europe's largest grain producer and a key supplier to world markets, especially of bread-making wheat.

Grain traders said increasing evidence of another bumper crop this year helped to trigger a U-turn in European Commission policy on Thursday, when it abandoned a controversial export tax meant to safeguard wheat supplies for domestic consumers.
--Tim Hepher, Valerie Parent, Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146 teh
